record.body: Anthrophony is the layer of sound humans make: road traffic, aircraft, construction machinery, sirens, music, and voices, including the low-frequency rumble of engines and the broadband roar of highways. Anthrophony is the youngest layer in evolutionary terms, and it is also the loudest in many modern soundscapes, masking animal calls, disrupting breeding choruses, and changing how animals use a habitat. Unlike geophony, anthrophony follows human schedules: rush hours, flight paths, and work shifts, so its pattern in a soundscape reveals human activity as clearly as biophony reveals animal activity. This record covers anthrophony alone, kept distinct from the biophony it masks and the geophony it overlays.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Anthrophony: The Human-Made Layer'
import math
A = 70
B = 40
tot = 10 * math.log10(10 ** (A / 10.0) + 10 ** (B / 10.0))
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Level one: %.1f decibels' % A)
print('Level two: %.1f decibels' % B)
print('Combined level: %.1f decibels' % tot)
print('Note: decibels add logarithmically, never by plain addition.')
demo.expected_output:
Record: Anthrophony: The Human-Made Layer
Level one: 70.0 decibels
Level two: 40.0 decibels
Combined level: 70.0 decibels
Note: decibels add logarithmically, never by plain addition.
